turn_text: We start with Mike Johnson, congressman from Louisiana's 4th congressional district.
It's nice to talk with you. Let's start with the civility oath that you have been promoting on Capitol Hill to try to get more harmony in the trenches. How is that going?

You know, it's going very, very well. The origin of this commitment to civility document that everyone's talking about actually began back in January. I'm one of 55 new members of Congress. Clay Higgins and I were elected at the same time from Louisiana and we joined 55 or 53 others from around the country. And we all had a retreat right after we took our oaths of office in the first week of January that weekend. They put us on an Amtrak train, Jim, and they sent us to a colonial Williamsburg, put us all in a hotel together for three days so we could bond. So we did. It was very productive. And on the last day as we were leaving, all 55 new members of Congress sat around a U-shaped table in a meeting room. And we sent all the staff and media and family and everyone else out. And we just visited for about an hour and a half. And everybody sort of shared their heart. And it was remarkable because everyone articulated in their own words basically the same message. They said, I'm really disgusted with the way Washington is run. I hate the tone of the city. And I came here to do it differently. And so I was so moved by that, Tim, because everybody said the same thing. I thought, we all agreed to work together cooperatively in that setting. But I thought, this is going to change pretty quickly when we get back to the Capitol Hill because there's some very contentious debates and obviously it's a difficult environment right now. So I went back to my office when we got back to town and I just one page document commitment to stability basically articulating its principles. And in summary, we would do just simple things, show proper respect to one another and everyone else and encourage productive dialogue and model civility and our public and private actions. Pretty simple stuff.
